title: Kids Get More Screen Time When Parents Are Stressed
paragraphs: Many parents worry about how much time their children spend looking at screens. However, a new study from the United States suggests that one of the biggest factors behind children's screen time may be their parents' stress.

The study was carried out by researchers at Florida International University's Center for Children and Families, led by doctoral student Enid Moreira and assistant professor Shayl Griffith. It was published in the journal Family Relations in 2026. The researchers surveyed 822 parents and caregivers across the United States who had children aged between four and eight.

The researchers found that parents who were under more stress were more likely to use screens to calm their children or keep them busy. They were also less likely to set consistent limits on screen time. In particular, parents who felt emotionally distressed were less likely to enforce rules about screen use, while parents who felt overwhelmed by their child's behavior were more likely to give their child a screen during difficult moments.

According to Moreira, what stood out was the importance of caregivers' own stress in decisions about how children use screens. This suggests that parents need support just as much as their children do.

However, the researchers do not believe that using a screen to get through a difficult moment is necessarily harmful. Instead, they suggest focusing on the quality of what children watch, rather than only reducing the number of minutes. Parents are encouraged to choose media that is meaningful, engaging and suitable for their child's age. According to Griffith, when caregivers have the resources they need, they are better able to set consistent boundaries.

It is important to note that the study looked at families at only one point in time, so it cannot show which came first, the stress or the screen use. For example, children's behavior may affect both.

A separate study from Sheffield Hallam University in the UK also found a link between parents' stress and children's screen time. It also suggested that stressed parents who spend more time on their own phones may set an example for their children.
